title-proc.eng: Overview Report of the Fourth European Survey of Enterprises on New and Emerging Risks (ESENER 2024)

description-proc.eng: In 2024 EU-OSHA ran the fourth European Survey of Enterprises on New and Emerging Risks (ESENER 2024) with the aim of providing nationally comparable information on how workplaces across Europe manage health and safety. Substantial analyses of the results of the three previous waves of ESENER, carried out in 2009, 2014 and 2019, have provided a valuable insight into how occupational safety and health (OSH) is managed in practice across Europe; what the main drivers and barriers are; how stress, violence and harassment are managed; the use of digital technologies and its impact on the health and safety of employees ; and how employees are involved. ESENER 2024 has maintained the methodological changes implemented back in 2014 and the questionnaires since then are largely the same too, which enables trend analyses. In each of the three previous waves of ESENER, EU-OSHA published an Overview report of the findings , showing the main results by country, activity sector and size class for the four sections of the survey: OSH management, Psychosocial risk management, Drivers and barriers to OSH, and Worker participation. This call for tender invites bids for the development of an in-depth analysis of the ESENER 2024 findings, including a comparison with those of ESENER 2014 and 2019, that will lead to an Overview Report.

The scheme includes the provision of segregated cycle facilities, improved pedestrian facilities (footpath and junction upgrades), ducting, carriageway resurfacing, etc.. The scheme also includes the upgrade of three signal-controlled junctions to improve pedestrian and cyclist facilities; the three junctions are at Belvedere Place, Fitzgibbon Street and Summerhill. It also ties into two further junctions at Dorset Street Lower and at Amiens Street (The Five Lamps) junction. The scheme comprises the following:- Reconfiguration of Carriageway for Inclusion of Cycle Lanes - Site Clearance - Pavement Works - Kerbs and Footways - Traffic Islands - Public Lighting - Traffic Signs and Road Markings - Drainage Works - Traffic Signals and Ducting - Utilities - Landscaping and Public Realm Works - Bus Shelters (foundations only) - Bike Stands - Temporary Traffic Management. description-proc.eng: A direct procurement of licences for a SaaS system (service) STATdx with the supplier Elsevier.Helse Nord RHF needs a regional, time-limited agreement on access to clinical radiological decision support/entry work for radiologists and LIS doctors. The procurement will be assessed as a procurement without a competition pursuant to the procurement regulations § 5-2 first section letter a, as the procurement, according to the contracting authority ́s assessment, can only be made with one specific supplier in the market. The need concerns a ready established SaaS/web based content service with medical quality assured radiology content, structured diagnostic support, differential diagnostics and a comprehensive case and picture library across radiological disciplines and modalities. The procurement does not apply to a general learning platform, course platform or technical portal, but to complete clinical radiological decision support content that can be used immediately without customer driven content production, quality assurance and management. Helse Nord has carried out a market survey, including RFI and dialogue with radiological environments. Identified alternatives are wetting among different LMS/platform systems. These systems do not currently appear as functionally equivalent substitutes, as they do not document finished medical quality assured radiological decision support content to the necessary extent and quality. Based on the market survey (RFI) and the substitute evaluation, Helse Nord ́s assessment is that STATdx from Elsevier is the only identified system that fulfils the necessary and proportional minimum requirements for the limited service at the current time. The agreement is limited to a bridge period of 1+1+1 years to ensure continuity, at the same time that Helse Nord maintains room for action to assess the market and any future alternatives.

title-proc.eng: 10024964-Sustainable Economic Opportunities for Youth in Turkana West and Lokichoggio

description-proc.eng: Kenya hosts over 830,000 refugees and asylum seekers (UNHCR, December 2025), with 36% living in Kakuma camp and Kalobeyei settlements of Turkana West sub-county. Poverty affects 72% of the sub-county"s hosting community of around 240,000 people and 58% of the refugee population (KNBS, 2022) The youth, especially young women and refugees in protracted displacement situation, face significant barriers to acquiring skills, income, and economic self-reliance, resulting in strong dependency on humanitarian aid and other support services. The project Promoting Employability and Entrepreneurship in Turkana West and Lokichoggio (ProSEET) pursues the objective to strengthen the socio-economic self-reliance of youth in the refugee and host communities. On behalf of the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) follows an integrated approach to sustainable employment in Turkana West. ProSEET project cooperates with local training institutions, business skills training providers, business associations, and local authorities at a structural level. In its three fields of action, ProSEET takes a holistic approach to employment promotion and simultaneously addresses multiple barriers to employment and economic participation affecting both the refugee and hosting communities: Action Area 1 improves the conditions for socio-economic self-reliance of youth in the refugee and host communities, by sharing labor market information through listening groups, game shows, mobile counselling services and digital campaigns. These activities also cover remote areas of the sub-county providing access to information. Action Area 2 addresses access to employment-oriented skills training for youth by strengthening the capacities of local trainers and institutions, introducing new qualifications, and offering technical and entrepreneurial courses. Action Area 3 focuses on building the capacities of local government and private-sector stakeholders to expand their business-related services and provide target-group-specific support for microentrepreneurs, aiming to boost MSME competitiveness, incomes, and create jobs. Activities include public-private dialogues, financial literacy and entrepreneurial skills trainings for micro and small enterprises, promotion of loan and saving groups (especially among women-headed households) and supporting start-ups through business incubation, mentorship, and grants.

title-proc.eng: Market Dialogue notice: Kymenlaakso Rescue Department – DIGIMARIS Project_Oil Spill Response Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) for Coastal Operations

description-proc.eng: Background Kymenlaakso Rescue Department (KRD) is preparing the possible acquisition of an Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) for operational oil spill response in coastal and archipelago environments. The preparation is carried out within the DIGIMARIS project funded by the Interreg Central Baltic Programme. The purpose of this market dialogue is to improve the Contracting Authority's understanding of available technologies, integration approaches, operational limitations, delivery models, costs and life-cycle implications before launching a possible procurement procedure. KRD has not yet finalised the technical or commercial requirements for the potential future USV procurement. Suppliers and other market operators are therefore invited to provide information and comments on feasible operational performance, sensor integration, communication solutions, navigation and autonomy, maintenance concepts, information and cyber security, training, life-cycle services and other relevant aspects. KRD is particularly interested in understanding what can realistically be achieved with commercially available USV technology in coastal oil spill response operations and in Baltic Sea coastal and archipelago conditions. This notice constitutes a technical market dialogue and is not a call for tenders or a contract notice. The response is not a tender and does not bind the Contracting Authority or the respondent in any subsequent procurement procedure. The Contracting Authority is not obliged to proceed with the procurement. Information obtained through the market dialogue may be used in the preparation of a possible future procurement procedure. Operational Need The potential future USV is intended primarily for operational oil spill response. All other capabilities shall be considered supportive or optional unless otherwise specified. The potential future USV is expected to support the following tasks: • detection and monitoring of oil spills • provision of real-time situational awareness for incident command • operation in coastal and archipelago waters • remote operation from a vessel, shore or command centre • autonomous navigation along a predefined route • safe navigation and mission continuity during GNSS interference, spoofing or complete loss of the GNSS signal • hazardous gas assessment before rescue personnel approach the incident area • optional support for environmental monitoring and water rescue operations • optional deployment of containment booms or integration of other oil spill response equipment The Contracting Authority is seeking information on complete solutions as well as relevant platforms, payloads, sensors, software, integrations and life-cycle services. Respondents may propose a complete solution or identify the parts of the solution that they are able to provide. Market Dialogue Response Respondents shall complete the attached DIGIMARIS USV Technical Market Dialogue Response Workbook. The completed workbook and any supporting attachments shall be submitted in English through the Supplier Portal by the stated deadline. The respondent shall be responsible for all costs related to the preparation and submission of its response. The Contracting Authority may request clarifications concerning the information submitted. Any requests for clarification or further dialogue will be conducted in a transparent and non-discriminatory manner. Demonstrations and Trials KRD may invite respondents to present their solutions and, where feasible, to participate in operational demonstrations or trials in Finland. Demonstrations may include remote operation, autonomous navigation, oil detection, gas monitoring, situational awareness and operation in communications or GNSS-degraded conditions. Participation in demonstrations or trials will not provide an advantage in any possible future procurement procedure. No compensation will be paid for participation unless otherwise agreed separately in writing. Participation in the market dialogue, a presentation, demonstration or trial does not constitute a prerequisite for participation in any possible future procurement procedure.

description-proc.eng: The purpose of this contract is to provide technical assistance for the implementation, coordination, monitoring and strategic support of two European Union funded regional maritime security programmes in SubSaharan Africa: one covering the Western Indian Ocean and one covering the Red Sea/Horn of Africa. The services shall support the effective, coherent and visible delivery of programme activities, reinforce coordination among implementing partners and stakeholders, and contribute to the sustainability of the regional maritime security architecture. It shall cover five interlinked objectives: 1. To ensure effective coordination, supervision and coherence of actions implemented at programme level, including complementarity and synergies among implementing partners. 2. To strengthen effective ownership of programme activities at country and regional level. 3. To strengthen coordination and cooperation between regional and national partners and the Regional Coordination Operations Centre (RCOC) and Regional Maritime Information Fusion Centre (RMIFC). 4. The expected outputs of this contract are as follows: 1.1 The supervision of implementation of activities and the coordination of the work between the different implementing partners is ensured at programme level. 1.2 The joint planning and information sharing practices to support coherent implementation at programme level and across the two programmes is strengthened. 1.3 The coherence, complementarity and strategic alignment between the two programmes and implementing partners is strengthened. 2.1 The engagement of national and regional stakeholders in the planning, implementation and follow-up of activities is ensured at programme level. 2.2 A mechanism to ensure follow-up, accountability and sustained engagement in programme implementation is established. 3.1 Information sharing between national actors and the RMIFC and RCOC is strengthened. 3.2 Sustainable partnerships and mutual trust between national and regional stakeholders and the two centres is improved. 4.1 A comprehensive results-based monitoring system is established and applied at programme level. 4.2 Timely, accurate and comprehensive reporting by the implementing partners is ensured at programme level. 4.3 The programmes are adjusted and steered on a need-to basis, informed by evidence and analytical insights. 5.1 The activities of the two programmes are systematically aligned with relevant EU policies, strategies and initiatives. 5.2 Synergies and complementarities between different EU interventions are identified and operationalised. 5.3 Structured information sharing and communication with EU institutions and stakeholders is ensured. Tasks shall include support to planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, communication, knowledge management and coordination with implementing partners, donors, regional organisations, national authorities and relevant international actors. description-proc.eng: The Creative Climate Action Fund III (2026-2029) is a key deliverable for the Creative Climate Action and Sustainability pillar of the Creative Ireland Programme. This fund seeks to build on the premise that transformational action on climate change requires cultural change throughout society, and with the ambition to utilise the potential of the arts, creativity and heritage to inspire and empower the culture change needed to transform to a net zero Ireland by 2050. A key finding of the evaluation of the first fund was the need for training and development of project leaders to ensure that this investment realises the object of building enduring capacity in the sector. There will be organisations from different sectors in receipt of the grant funding including: arts and cultural organisations, local authorities, research institutions, environmental groups and community development organisations. However, a consistency of understanding of the policy objectives and best-practice methods of project delivery will be essential to the success of the fund. Therefore, this training and development package will: * Ensure a consistency of technical knowledge across all project teams * Ensure a consistency of approach to be taken on dialogue between projects and with communities the projects are engaging and facilitating dialogue with, to ensure that this aligns with the approach taken in the National Dialogue on Climate Action (NDCA) * Ensure full understanding of the policy framework as set out in the Climate Action Plan 2025. * Support individual projects in their approach to data collection and evaluation * Support project management and communications functions within individual projects * Provide a supportive network for the projects to facilitate collaboration and sharing of skills, knowledge and best practice It is envisaged that that the training will be delivered in a mixture of in person and online settings. Most of the elements of this training and development will be delivered in a initial residential workshop setting to assist the fund recipients to develop their networks. This is particularly important for this fund, due to the cross-sectoral nature of the partnerships. While the tender will seek a private sector provider, it is envisaged that the Creative Ireland Programme will work with the provider and utilise public sector capacity in the co-creation of the training materials and training delivery including possible guest speakers (i.e. Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment (DCEE), the Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI), Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)).

title-proc.eng: 10022598-Short-Term Expert Pools to support negotiations and implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)

description-proc.eng: Background: Although many of the world"s fastest-growing economies are in Africa, trade among African countries remains limited. The continent mostly exports raw materials and agricultural products, while it imports machinery, equipment, and food mainly from outside Africa. The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which is one of the African Union"s (AU) flagship projects for the implementation of its Agenda 2063, aims to change this. It is expected that, with the introduction of the free trade zone, intra- African trade will be 15% to 25% higher by 2040 (UNECA). The AfCFTA agreement has been signed by 54 of the 55 African Union Member States (MS) and became effective under international law in May 2019. The full implementation of the AfCFTA will lead to a continental single market of more than 1.4 billion people with an aggregate GDP exceeding USD 2 trillion. Our Approach: The GIZ implemented project "Support to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) II" cofinanced by the BMZ and the EU, seeks to improve framework conditions for the realisation of the AfCFTA and supports the outstanding negotiations and the implementation of the AfCFTA. For this, the programme supports the African Union, specifically the Department for Economic Development, Trade, Tourism, Industry, Minerals (ETTIM) and the AfCFTA Secretariat at the continental level in the coordination of AfCFTA implementation. On the regional level the programme cooperates with Regional Economic Communities (RECs), specifically EAC (East African Community), ECOWAS (Economic Community for West African States) and SADC (South African Development Community, plus additional RECs based on request). The programme also supports Member States (Ethiopia, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, Tunisia, Zambia, plus additional Member States based on request) by working with national institutions, like trade ministries and customs, to implement the agreement. Lastly, the programme works closely with private sector and civil society actors to increase trade under the AfCFTA. Together with the named partners, the programme covers interventions across all technical areas of the AfCFTA. The EU co-financed part of the programme, the EU Technical Assistance Facility, operates as a multi-partner contribution agreement between the European Commission, GIZ (lead implementing agency), Expertise France, and FIAP. A Project Management Unit, which is housed in the AfCFTA Secretariat, oversees the implementation of the programme and the execution of activities.
